Noodle Incident: Whatever it was that happened between him and Pinako long ago has him terrified of her. He practically lapses into PTSD when Winry asks about it, and he refuses to elaborate. This was strangely left out of Brotherhood despite being sourced from the manga.

characters.name: Paninya
characters.description: A girl from Rush Valley who meets Ed in an arm-wrestling competition prior to her stealing Ed’s watch. Adaptational Badass: Her missing arm aside, this Paninya lacks her counterpart's fear of blood. Adaptational Heroism: Her personality and motives aren't exactly different from the manga/Brotherhood, but this Paninya hasn't resorted to thievery when we first meet her and instead tries repaying Dominic to bring his shop prestige by showcasing his automail in a (seemingly) legitimate contest. Her stealing Ed’s watch is made to be a scheme connived with Winry to teach him a lesson in good automail (without cheating via alchemy) and to help Paninya with gaining some good exposure by outpacing a State Alchemist. It's inferred she didn't intend to actually pawn off the watch even if she had thrown Ed off her tail. Adaptational Wimp: She lost her right arm in addition to both legs in the '03 anime.Downplayed somewhatin regard to her automail in that while she lacks her leg blade here, she retains herLeg Cannon. Ambiguously Brown: Of a different variety than the folks of Lior, though unlike the aforementioned people, she is also dark-skinned in the original continuity.

characters.name: Gold Steiner
characters.description: Gold Steiner is the older brother of the famed alchemist Silver Steiner, who had died by 1897 when Izumi Harnet sought him out. While Silver was well known for his master alchemy skill, Gold was famous for his hand-to-hand combat abilities. Eyes Always Shut: He has intimidating black eyes when opened Retired Badass: That's considering how he was willing to put a young Izumi throughTraining from Hell. And even though he isn't as famous as his brother, he is considered well known for his martial arts prowess.

characters.name: Julia Crichton
characters.description: Thetritagonistof the animatedNon-Serial MovieFullmetal Alchemist: The Sacred Star of Milos. She is an alchemist from the Death Valley underground below Table City, as well as affiliated with an organization there called the Black Bats. An Arm and a Leg:Loses a leg in the final battle after using the Sanguine Star and crossing the Gate to save her brother. Canon Foreigner: Both in the trope sense and in the meta sense with her country itself being this trope. Combat Medic: Her alchemy revolves around healing, and she is no slouch in a fight. Determinator: Nothing will stop her from trying to save the valley.

characters.name: Führer President King Bradley
characters.description: The ruler of Amestris. He simultaneously serves as the country's chief executive (president) and commander-in-chief (Führer) — and to clear any confusion, King is simply his first name. He came to rule Amestris after leading his nation out of a bloody civil war and setting up a military dictatorship.He is later revealed to be the homunculus Pride, and inThe Movie, it turns out he'sthe alternate universe's version ofFritz Lang. Adaptational Attractiveness: He looks a bit younger than his manga counterpart and his mustache is less prominent. He also has softer-looking features.This is probably due to him representing Pride instead of Wrath, and indeed, it manages to cover up his true nature much better. Adaptational Badass:Zig-Zagged. Bradley lacks the main weakness of his manga counterpart;2003 Bradley has aHealing Factorlike the other homunculi, while manga!Bradley does not due to being a converted human. As such,Mustang burning him alive would have killed his manga counterpart, while this Bradley can recover from it. That said, anime Bradley also has a new weakness in the form ofhis human remains, which leads to his defeat. Manga Bradley also has many more badass moments on-camera than anime Bradley, including defeating Mustang. Adaptational Dumbass: A very rare, justified example:He represents Pride instead of Wrath, so him taunting and drawing out the fight withBond Villain Stupiditymakes sense, as a prideful person would want to gloat and make things last for the sake of bolstering his ego. His manga counterpart, however, wastes no time in disabling Mustang due to embodying a far much vicious sin. Adaptational Villainy: While Bradley in the manga andBrotherhoodwas still an evil man, he still retains some noble qualities, like his love for his wife. Here, not so much.It gets to the point where he snaps the neck of his young son Selim when the latter unintentionally brought him his remains while fighting Mustang.

characters.name: Frank Archer
characters.description: An official from the military court who replaces Maes Hughes after his untimely death. Unlike his predecessor, he is an incredibly cold and vicious man and is known for his love of war. Arm Cannon:After his restructuring, his mechanical arm features a built-in machine gun. Artificial Limbs:One arm and leg. The former has a machine gun attached. Ax-Crazy: By the end of the series, Archer has completely lost whatever was left of his sanity, gunning down his subordinates along with the rebels while cackling in glee. Bad Boss:He doesn't mind gunning down his own soldiers following his reconstruction as an automail cyborg.

characters.name: Vato Falman, Kain Fuery, and Heymans Breda
characters.description: Mustang's other subordinates, a trio of officers that fill out various functions. Their loyalty to Mustang is unquestionable. Adaptational Early Appearance: Falman makes his debut here on the train heist headed by Bald and the Blue Squad alongside Maes Hughes whereas the manga equivalent only has him appearing at the end behind Mustang with the other two plus Havoc. Adaptational Wimp: Even worse than Havoc, who at least was shown fighting in the coup. They are practically shown as desk jockeys. In the original, while this was their primary job, they often rushed to the scene to provide backup, and they were directly used in field missions to engage the enemy or provide essential support roles (in particular during the attempt to capture homunculi). Big, Thin, Short Trio: Breda is big, Falman is thin and Fuery is short. Brilliant, but Lazy: Hinted at with Breda, considering his skill at strategy games.

characters.name: Adolf Hitler
characters.description: Yes,him; the one and only. The leader of the burgeoning National Socialist German Workers’ Party and future leader ofGermany. He acts as theGreater-Scope VillaininConqueror of Shamballa, employing hateful rhetoric and ruthless, brutal tactics in his plans to seize control of the country and conquer all the lands. Absolute Xenophobe: He despises anyone who doesn’t fit his Aryan ideals of having features such as white skin, blonde hair and blue eyes as well as only coming from a certain ethnic background. He pretty much embodies nearly every trope about discrimination and prejudice. Alternate Self: Appears to be this toPride/King Bradley.Subvertedsince it’s actuallyFritz Langwho’s Bradley’s counterpart. Ax-Crazy: He’s certainly always been off his rockerto say the least. The Corrupter:Serves as this to Maes Hughes’s counterpart and many others, presumably even inspiring Noah’s fellow gypsies to turn against her.Histeachingswill continue poisoning people well into the future.

characters.name: Dietlinde Eckhart
characters.description: The chairwoman of the Thule Society, the secretive occult research arm of the future Nazi government. She acts as the primary antagonist ofConqueror of Shamballa. Eckhart aims to open a portal to Amestris — to her, the fabled "Shamballa" — so she can use its "magic" to help Hitler take over Germany. However, upon realizing the true power of the alternative world's alchemists Eckhart's excitement turns to paranoia, driving her to instead try to destroy the other world out of fear they may conquer her own. Absolute Xenophobe: Unsurprisingly as a pro-Aryan supporter of the Nazi party. Despite her goal to wield the power of the titular Shamballa she begins to fear the strength of alchemy, decidesthe denizens of the other world are untrustworthy beasts and tries to kill them all. Alternate Self:Possibly to Dante given the resemblance to her son Envy’s original human form and similar worldviews. And There Was Much Rejoicing: Officer Hughes,upon her corpse reverting back to its normal state, looksrelievedupon realizing the true identity of the “monster” he killed.Nobody else mourns her either, not even her otherwise loyal dragon Rudolf Hess. Ax-Crazy:Devolves into this after crossing throught the Gate and arriving at Amestris, rambling about how she is going todestroy their entire worldout of fear and paranoia. She also acts incredibly unhinged during the final confrontation against Edward and before her death.

characters.name: Noah
characters.description: A young Romani woman whom Ed encounters in our world. All of the Other Reindeer: So much thatshe aids the Thule Society thinking that, if she reaches Amestris, she won't be discriminated against there. Given her jerkass "fellow" gypsies remorselessly sell her to a carnival and she only weakly complains to them (who brush it off and depart without looking back), this is made scathingly obvious that there was no camaraderie there. Worse, those other gypsies never appear again and sufferno consequencesfor selling her out. Alternate Self: Implied to be Rosé Thomas' Earth counterpart. Unlike with Rosé, she has no pink highlights on her front bangs. Big "NO!":Upon seeing Ed returning to “Shamballa”, she screams after him to come back and take her with him before shouting this. I Choose to Stay:Ultimately does not join the Elrics on their future travels by the end, instead remaining behind with her newfound people/friends in Munich.

characters.name: Alfons Heiderich
characters.description: A boy whom Edward also becomes friends with in our world. He has a huge and beautiful dream and needs to fulfill it soon... because he's dying of an illness. Ambiguously Bi: There are many moments implying that his interest in Edward is more than platonic, such as when he makes a bothered face when Edward tells him how he can't wait to get back to his world (which means permanently leaving him). Though at the beginning of the movie, he is also seen blushing and flustered by the Romani women they meet after Ed wrecks their vehicle. Beware the Nice Ones:In the middle of the film, he comes back from work looking slightly disturbed, and when Edward right after that tries to convince him to get away from the Thule Society, Alfons shoves him to the stairs, yelling that he has no right to tell him what to do. Dies Wide Open:After being shot by Rudolf Hess. Dream Walker: Got this trope applied to him by Alphonse, who states that he often sees a 17-year-old version of himself staying with Edward in a strange world.

characters.name: Fritz Lang
characters.description: Yes,thatFritz Langand our world's counterpart to King Bradleynotetechnically the counterpart to the man Bradley/Pride was based on. He and Ed cross paths after a case ofMistaken Identity, and he goes on to act as a source of advice and aid through the movie. Big Damn Heroes: Charges his car into a pub filled with Nazi Party members in order to save Ed and help him in stopping the planned invasion of Amestris. Changed My Mind, Kid: Zigzagged, as while he is implied to ultimately escape from Germany at the film's denouement, he does rescue Edward from a Nazi-infested beer hall and aids the boy in getting to the factory where the Gate is going to be opened so Ed can thwart the villains' plans. Eccentric Mentor: To Ed. Good Counterpart: To King Bradley/Pride.

characters.name: Huskisson
characters.description: A villain that appears in the prologue of the film, framed during an adventure Ed and Al went on between the events of the series that Ed is telling Alfons Heiderich about in the present. Artificial Zombie: Huskissonattemptedto create an army of cybernetic walking corpses and unleash them on the Elrics once they disable his main drill. Being ahuman transmutation, this obviously fails and onlyrobs the loon of his own life. Bad Boss: Dismisses the workers who have died under his supervision mining the uranium as an unavoidable sacrifice in scientific process. The Elrics arenotamused by his callousness. Evil Gloating: Bit him in the ass as spelt out by Ed who only cared about his uranium discovery as a potential lead on the Philosopher's Stone. It didn't, of course, and they end up foiling him just so he won’t introduce more destructive weapons to the Amestris military. Incompletely Trained: Implied; His ability to summon the Gate while attempting to revive his fallen workers implies that Huskisson's skill in alchemic study could have been something else should he had pursued it further (human transmutation, even failed attempts, are seen as very difficult to perform).

characters.name: Armony Eiselstein
characters.description: Artificial Human:She is described as a unique kind of human chimera due to being fused with Selene. Crash-Into Hello: The way she meets the Elrics. Armony tries to pick some Etherflowers at the top on the mountain but falls down and lands directly on Edward's face. Died in Your Arms Tonight:She and her father Wilhelm die as he embraces her. Ethereal White Dress:Wears this in the ending. Fiery Redhead: Nearly picks a fight with three street thugs who arealchemistsby herself. Odds are she would’ve lost spectacularly had Ed and Al not shown up.

characters.name: Wilhelm Eiselstein
characters.description: Fantasy-Forbidding Father: He refuses to teach alchemy to Armony and has forbidden every other alchemist in the town from doing it either.Turns out he has good reasons for doing so, because her body serves as host to the Philosopher's Catalyst, which makes it extremely fragile and unstable.

characters.name: Edward "Ed" Elric
characters.description: The protagonist of the series. Ed seeks the secret of the Philosopher's Stone so he can undo the mistakes of his past of trying to bring his mother back to life. The truth behind the Philosopher's Stone and the connection to the secrets behind the country he lives in drives the story. Adaptational Angst Upgrade:Ed’s more brooding than in the manga, or at least seems to be. This is because the writing focuses on current events rather than dwelling on his backstory — this version of Edward is faced with problems that require imperfect, morally questionable solutions and frequently confronted with the consequences of his decisions.In relation to this he instead learns that his actions,no matter how well-intentionedended up causing far more harm than good in the long runand that he and his brother were actually manipulated into their journey rather than doing it of their own free will.In the manga Ed moves past his guilt upon discoveringwhat he and Al created in their human transmutationwasn’ttheir mother and in turn deduces a way to restore Al's body from this revelation. It doesn't happen in this version of the story because human transmutation works differently and result in the birth of ahomunculus— instead of an immobile freak that died instantly, Ed and Al created Sloth, who looks identical to their mother. So when Ed comes face-to-face with his original mistake it's in a much more violent, tragic way. Even the context of Ed exhuming a grave illustrates this contrast; in the manga he digs up the transmuted body from his and Al’s attempt to verify it isn't their mother while here he unearths his mother’s grave to get a part of her body so he can use it toweakenand kill Sloth.His adherence toThou Shalt Not Killbreaks down painfully over the course of the story, starting with himaccidentally killing Greed. Thisdrives him into hystericsand serves as the first step towards him taking a darker path than his manga counterpart which culminates in him killing said homuncul

characters.name: Alphonse "Al" Elric
characters.description: Edward's younger brother, he lost his body during an experiment that went horribly wrong. He survives in the form of a suit of armor, his soul joined to it through the use of a blood seal. The Ace: InConqueror of Shamballahe's become a State Alchemist just like Edward had and possesses unique abilities even amongst other alchemists due to having looked into the Gate. Achilles' Heel: It's pretty much impossible to do any permanent harm to him since his metal body can just be transmuted back together after sustaining any damage. The only way to kill him is to damage the blood seal binding his soul to his suit of armor body... at least until hebecomes a Philosopher’s Stone, at which point even falling into a river doesn’t erase it. In exchange however,exhausting the Philosopher's Stone's power will exhaust Al's life force as well. Adaptation Dye-Job: His hair changes from blond like his brother's to dark blond. His eyes are also hazel here as opposed to gold in the manga. Adaptational Angst Upgrade:In particular, his dilemma over whether his memories are real lasts longer and is explored a lot more.Like Ed, he has to deal with the fact that their attempt athuman transmutationcreated ahomunculusin the image of their mother instead of athingthat couldn’t even function.He ends uphousing the Philosopher's Stone itself and thus becomes a prime target by those seeking its power.He learns that his brother’s been trapped in a world that functions differently, accidentally allows an invasion from said world to enter his own and ends up having to stay in that same world permanently.

characters.name: Wrath
characters.description: A hot-tempered, needy child first discovered by Ed in a feral state who underwent aFace–Heel Turnthanks to Envy. He is the failed transmutation of Izumi Curtis' dead son. Wrath’s introduction is roughly when the series' narrative completely breaks away from the manga's. Ambiguous Innocence: As aWild Child, Wrath is completely ignorant of social norms before hisHeel–Face Turn. For one thing, he can't seem to understand the difference between being dead and asleep. And I Must Scream: Being trapped beyond the Gate was not a fun experience for him. Antagonistic Offspring: To Izumi, for sure.Technically one for Ed as well, given the latter's unintended role in bringing him to life.

characters.name: Dr. Tim Marcoh
characters.description: A State Alchemist who served in Ishbal and creator of the red stones. Due to his experience in the war, he deserts the military, living a quiet life as a country doctor until trouble comes knocking on his door. Adaptational Attractiveness: He never gets deformed by Scar in this version. Adaptational Early Appearance: In the manga andBrotherhood, the Elrics meet Marcoh by chance while heading back to Risembool to recuperate from Scar's ambush. Here, they're specifically looking for the doctor before Ed's battle with Scar. In fact, in this version, Scar attackswhilethe brothers are with Marcoh and the doctor threatens Scar with the Philosopher's Stone. Adaptational Wimp: Unlike his mainline counterpart, this Marcoh remains, for the most part, a guilt-ridden, traumatized, and altogether paranoid man as he never gets the chance to develop further beyond Ed encouraging him to flee which is quickly thwarted. Anything but That!: Hysterically begs not to be taken back to Lab 5 for more human experimentation as Grand’s men drag him away. Thankfully, a combination of Scar's sudden attack and the Elrics' interference spare himfor the time being.

characters.name: The Slicer Brothers
characters.description: A duo of serial killing brothers who terrorized Central years ago and were supposedly executed. In truth, they were experimented on, bound to a metal suit of armor and then tasked with guarding Laboratory 5. Actually Pretty Funny: The older brother can’t help but laugh at the irony of being treated as a human being despite being reduced to an immobile steel helmet once Ed defeats both him and the younger brother after them both having been treated as monsters their entire lives while they were still flesh and blood. What's notable is how the way he cackles is not at all meanspirited towards Ed’s rationale; he seems genuinely tickled by the idea. Adaptation Dye-Job: Similar to Envy's. Slicers' armor is red-colored in the 2003 anime but green inBrotherhood. Affably Evil: Both of them are surprisingly well-mannered and spoken for a pair of mass murderers, especially the older brother. Ambiguous Situation: It's unclear if the older brother also controls the body while he's attached to the younger brother, though their slightly different combat styles does imply that he can.

characters.name: DominicLeCoulte
characters.description: A gruff automail engineer from Rush Valley who took in Paninya and made her automail. He somehow knows Pinako Rockbell. Adaptational Nice Guy: Downplayed and zigzagged as while he isn't living a reclusive life in the mountains like the original version, his family is unmentioned (assuming they exist at all here) and he works in a back-alley repair shop in Rush Valley with only Paninya as his helper. Played straighter in that he's much more tolerant of having company as long as you're not disrespecting his craft and allows Winry to help Paninya fix her right arm without any complaints. He also seemingly agreed to take on Winry as his apprentice in the epilogue whereas he never caved to such demand in the manga/Brotherhood. Adaptational Wimp: Only by proxy as his impressive moment, going out into a storm to fetch a doctor to help with his daughter-in-law's giving birth, is excised. Otherwise, Dominic still gives a strong impression you don't want to push him. Adapted Out: His family is not present here with only Paninya being shown as his assistant. Badasses Wear Bandanas: Wears a light beige bandana during work hours or while tuning up his store's supply.

characters.name: Hohenheim of Light
characters.description: The Elrics' father, a renowned alchemist who left them and their mother when they were little. Adaptational Dumbass: While he is certainly no idiot,he didn't really have much of a plan against Dante other than just confronting her head-on, a decision that would proveveryunwise. His manga counterpart studies to find out what Father is up to and sets out taking procedures to counteract his plan. Adaptational Intelligence: In contrast to his original/Brotherhoodself, this Hohenheimseemed to become a master alchemist all on his own, without needing the assistance of the Dwarf in the Flask. Unfortunately, his motivations were significantly less humble, as he directly sought out the Philosopher's Stone rather than simply seek out freedom from slavery. Adaptational Jerkass: Unlike in the manga andBrotherhoodwherehe left his family for good reasons, here his motivations were entirely selfish;he didn't want Trisha and his children to realize who orwhathe was, so he abandoned them. He also abandoned his former family of Dante and Envy, the latter being the homunculus of his firstborn son. There's also the implications that he seduced Dante as his student, an action his original selfneverperformed in any regard. Adaptational Late Appearance: He only shows up at the tail-end of the story while in the manga andBrotherhoodhe reappears at the end of the first third. For reference, here he returns in episode 43 (out of 51) while in the manga it's chapter 40 (out of 108) and inBrotherhoodepisode 19 (out of 64).Justifiedsince the manga chapter reintroducing him was freshly published when the anime ended.

characters.name: Gracia Hughes
characters.description: The mother of Elicia and the adored wife of Maes Hughes. She gets a bit more of a prominent role inConqueror of Shamballa. Beware of the Nice Ones: Despite her obviously gentle nature she's not afraid tostand up to Hughes in the movie, though this is her counterpart. Caring Gardener: In the movie'salternate world, Earth, she's a florist and Hughes has a crush on her. Clean, Pretty Childbirth: Pretty much. Though, while we're not shown any graphic details, Gracia's shown to be in pain, and 11 and 12-year-old Ed and Al freak out over the likes of "what's necessary" during a birth such as hot water and cloth. Determined Expression: Has one defending Noah in the movie.

characters.name: Elicia Hughes
characters.description: The daughter of Gracia and Maes Hughes in the series. Age Lift: The 2003 anime adds a year to her age whenshe loses her father. Birth-Death Juxtaposition: In the first anime,her birth and Nina's death are juxtapositioned in the same arc. Born During a Storm: Gracia goes into labor during a snowstorm, which has Hughes run out trying to find a doctor for along time, to Ed, Al and Nina'sabsolute panic. Cheerful Child: She's shown to have grown up cheerful a few years after we first meet her as an extremely newborn baby.

characters.name: Lyra
characters.description: A young State Alchemist who serves as the enforcer of Lieutenant Yoki during her first appearance. Later on in the series, she reappears as the newest student of Dante. Battle Butler: In her first appearance, she's Yoki's maid as well as his personal bodyguard and enforcer. Blow You Away: She has wind-based alchemy powers. The Cameo: Shows up briefly in the movie asher parallel world counterpart. Canon Foreigner: She's exclusive to the 2003 series; notably, the episode which introduces her is an otherwise faithful adaptation of a manga chapter.

characters.name: Dante
characters.description: Formerly Izumi's alchemy teacher, now an elderly woman who lives in a mansion in the woods with her current student, Lyra. Badass Teacher: She is the one who taught Izumi alchemy, after all. Big Bad: Later on it is revealedDante is actually a 400-year old alchemist and Hohenheim's first lover with a severe case of God Complex, who aims to gather Philosopher's Stones to live forever throughBody Surfing, and for this creates or recruits Homunculi (under the false promise of turning them human) to instigate conflicts, spread diseases and manipulate alchemists and other people to forge a stone. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Implied. When we first see her, she appears to a wise, experienced old mentor who is willing to help the Elric brothers. However, she also had a pretty harsh falling-out with Izumi in the past that left evenIzumiin tears while Dante was absolutely stone-faced.She's also theBig Badand leader of the homunculi, so naturally, she plays this trope straight as as an arrow. The Cameo: Dante pops up in Episode 58 ofBrotherhood, as well as in the "Let's Nab Oprah!" episode ofThe Boondocks.

characters.name: The Chimeras / Devil's Nest Gang
characters.description: Law, Dorochet, Marta, and Bido. Half-human, half-animal beings created through illegal alchemical procedures, they worked for the military in specialist roles before finding much more fulfilling work withGreed. Adaptational Badass: Marta could only slither into tight spaces with her snake abilities in the manga, but here she can also use her arms like a powerful snake tail, as she demonstrates in her scuffle with Kimblee and showcased in the third opening against Edward. Adaptational Jerkass: A subtle case with Bido. In the manga he's only ever shown to be kind, naive, and innocent, but here he shows an interest in Kimblee's bombs and is a bit of aTroll. Adaptational Nice Guy: Marta. She's only antagonistic as long as Greed is and makes peace with the Elrics after he is defeated. Adaptation Dye-Job: Law's military coat is navy blue in this version and greenish beige in the manga. Dorochet’s hair color changed from black to dark blond. Marta is given green eyes as opposed to the bluish ones she has in the original story, and her tattoo is recolored magenta from the green it was initially.

characters.name: Nina Tucker
characters.description: Shou Tucker's 4-year-old daughter, usually seen with her large pet dog Alexander. She forms a sibling-like bond with the Elrics while they are staying at her home to study for their State Alchemy exam. Her father later transmutes her and Alexander into a chimera. After her transmutation, the State Military try to take her away, but the Elrics prevent this only for her to encounter Scar, who kills her out of mercy with his deconstruction alchemy.Her father spends the remainder of the series trying to revive her. Adaptational Badass: She and the Elrics help to deliver Elicia Hughes and while they're at it, she helps Ed discover he can use alchemy without a transmutation circle. Age Lift: Played with. While technically the same age as in the manga, since Nina meets the Elric brothers when Ed was studying to become a State Alchemist, she would have been 7 to 8 if she lived to the present here. Ascended Extra: Sort of. Appears in two episodes (implied to be several months at least) in the flesh and later asseveral creepy, lifeless dolls created by her father in many attempts to revive her, as well as in Ed's flashbacks and occasionally the end credits. Big Friendly Dog: Her dog Alexander, who's also her only friend prior to meeting the Elrics.

characters.name: Cornello
characters.description: The leader of the Church of Leto, a cult that controlled the town of Lior. In reality, he was a power-hungry alchemist whose "miracles" were actually performed with a Philosopher's Stone. Adaptational Badass: Mildly. He's still anUnwitting PawnandBig Bad Wannabeof the homunculi in this version, but he can also be genuinely intimidating (his chimeras, particularly the bird one, are genuinely horrific and he comes close to murdering Rose), unlike his manga andBrotherhoodversions where he's pretty much treated as just a pathetic huckster with an overinflated ego from the get. Here he only loses his menace and is treated as a joke following Ed's engineered public confession and in addition, he lasts longer here than he did inBrotherhood. Adaptational Jerkass: While he was already a hate sink in the manga, his cruelty is taken even further here when he creates a bird chimera to deceive Rosé into believing her deceased boyfriend has been revived, and then tries to murder Rosé with it. Asshole Victim: He is a cruel and smug manipulator who murders animals to be used as horrific weapons. Suffice to say, no one gives a shit when he ends up becoming Gluttony's dinner. Bad People Abuse Animals: Cornello has a long list of animal-related crimes of turning them into chimeras. Most horrific is the parrot-like one created from the souls of multiple birds that he used to impersonate the voice of Rose's dead fiancé, Cain, establishing Cornello as a grade-A piece of shit.

characters.name: Majhal
characters.description: The only alchemist from the small village of Linter and an old acquaintance of Van Hohenheim. He is well regarded by his fellow villagers, but hides a dark secret. All for Nothing: His kidnapping and murdering for the sake of making a new permanent Karin were all pointless as its revealed that the real Karin did not in fact die when she fell from a cliff and instead lost her memories and started a new life elsewhere, only regaining her sense of self twenty years later and came back hoping to be recognized by her Majhal. He was too far gone mentally by that point and obsessed with his own nostalgic memories of what could have been that he does not recognize “Lebi” until Ed spells it out. Even then, Majhal becomes enraged at the suggestion to the point he tries to murder them both for it, which only leads to his own demise and still refusing to acknowledge the old woman as his Karin, leaving behind a shattered shell of a lover. Ambiguous Situation: Supposedly was an old friend of Van Hohenheim's, but Majhal's later derision of the man as “stubborn” leaves to question if the two had a falling out over their differing philosophies on human alchemy. Majhal is not referenced again when Hohenheim makes his debut towards the end of the series, so it's a mystery. If Hohenheim's talk withDanteis any indication, he almost certainly would have thought even less of Majhal's actions. Ax-Crazy: He fully descended into madness when it's revealed that his accomplice Lebi was actually his beloved Karin now as an old woman close to his own age who never really died but suffered a head injury and lost her memories. He transmutes a sword from a screwdriver of his and charges her and Edward with the intent to kill them. Only Ed's quick thinking by transmuting a rose petal into a whip knocks the blade out of his hands,accidentally killing Majhal. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He seems like a soft-spokenCool Old Guyat first and is happy to advise the Elrics during their visit to Linter, havin

characters.name: Psiren
characters.description: Real name Clara. A thief who masquerades as a nurse, nun, and schoolteacher by day. The Elric brothers encounter her in Aquroya. Ambiguous Situation: Is Clara just yourrun-of-the-mill cat burglarusing Aquroya's treasures to live out her life? Does she even appreciate how her presence in the town is the only thing revitalizing an otherwise doomed city that is destined to sink under the waves in a few years' time? Al likes to believe in the latter, but Ed leans towards the former being closer to the truth. To her credit, Psiren does go out of her way not to seriously injure anybody, let alone kill them, including the cops pursuing her, and is also aGraceful Loserwhen she's finally apprehended. Anti-Villain: She's mostly unapologetically a thief, but never seriously injuries anybody, let alone murders, and at most acts like a tease towards Ed. An Aquroya citizen tells the Elrics that Psiren's presence has revitalized the town's economy since the settlement only has a few more years before the waters reclaim it and most of the original inhabitants abandoned it. Whether or not Psiren herself appreciates this is never really clear. Calling Card: Always announces her heists before moving in on the goods. It's implied that it's so her admirers can catch a glimpse of Psiren doing her job. Classy Cat-Burglar: The kindly nurse Clara is actually the master thief Psiren who is adored by Aquroya's masses for revitalizing their town after the majority of the original population abandoned their home due to flooding. Ironically enough, she utilizes water alchemy for her heists.

characters.name: The Tringham Brothers
characters.description: Two brothers who Ed and Al meet in the town of Xenotime while investigating rumors of the Philosopher's Stone. The boys pose as the Elrics in order to get support from the town, so that they may continue their father's research in making the stone. However, it turns out their father, Nash Tringham, abandoned the research as it involved using pregnant women to help with the process which was killing the town's newborns. He wound up killed by the scientist who was working alongside him (who was later revealed to be manipulated by Lust) and tricked the brothers into continuing the research. The two have a change of heart after realizing the truth and help the Elrics stop the scientist. Later, the Tringham brothers point the Elric brothers to where they can find a better lead. They have a short cameo later in the series. Russell Tringham is the elder sibling, while Fletcher Tringham is the younger. Berserk Button: Russell's appears to be anyone accusing him of never being able to live up to his dad's expectations, albeit not realizing that Nash had abandoned his research for good reasons and never would have wanted either of his sons to continue forward with it. Fletcher calling him out on pushing on in spite of bringing suffering to Xenotime and Mugear later letting it slip he murdered their dad for refusing to use fetuses to make more stones finally makes him see reason. Call to Agriculture: The Tringham brothers end their two-parter going to work on Belsio's lemon farm in order to help Xenotime stabilize without the aid of the Philosopher's Stone. Canon Foreigner: The brothers do not appear in the manga or theBrotherhoodanime. They do, however, appear in the first light novel,Fullmetal Alchemist: The Land of Sand, which is not written by Hiromu Arakawa but is set in the manga universe (written by Makoto Inoue). Comic-Book Fantasy Casting: Russell's appearance was modeled after the lateRiver Phoenix, as noted in the ancillary section of the light novel he debuted in.

characters.name: Mugear
characters.description: A greedy gold mine owner near the city of Xenotime who wants to create the Philosopher's Stone and employs the Tringham brothers to do so. Asshole Victim: Considering the fact that this guy let a nearby city be poisoned,killed the Tringhams' fatherand is a greedy bastard, it's hard to really mourn him. Disproportionate Retribution: Subverted. He seemingly imprisons the Tringham brothers just for Russell lightly refusing the “contingency plan” ofusing fetusesfor stone ingredients, but with the real Elrics having stumbled upon his scheme and Lust threatening to pull the plug on the whole operation,he was likely going to kill them sooner than later regardless. Evil Old Folks: Like Cornello before him, Mugear is up there in the years and is willing to take his money-grabbing extremes to deadly limits.He murdered Nash Tringham for refusing to go along with his fetus stone plan and tries to kill both the Tringhams and Elrics once they discover the truth. There’s also his willingly allowing Xenotime to be slowly poisoned to death by red watertwice! Fat Bastard: He's heavyset and no less of a nasty piece of work, going as far as wanting to taint pregnant women's unborn fetuses to use as stone materials.

characters.name: Lujon
characters.description: An alchemist who bears an uncanny resemblance to Scar's older brother. Lust met him when Envy unleashed an epidemic in his village and took on the role of teaching him so as to push him into creating the Philosopher's Stone. During this time, he fell in love with her. Two years later he seeks out Lust again... and it doesn't end well for him. All for Nothing: It turns out the fossil plague was engineered by Envy with the groundwork being conducted by Lust to drive Lujon or any other potential alchemist into being desperate enough to create the Philosopher's Stone. But the kindhearted Lujon never left his home village and actually sought after Lust again to gain a new stone to cure the villagers and hopefully be with her. Instead,she kills him and derides him as a mistake on her part. His stone is destroyed and all of the symptoms of the disease return without mercy, killing everybody and leaving the settlement a ghost town. Lydia also dies moments after returning to the village, the Elrics and Winry finding her corpse next to Lujon's. All-Loving Hero: He is dedicated to helping and curing others via alchemy. Just before he reunites with Lust, he stopped to help heal a boy who was injured in a carriage accident. Badass Boast: A sadly vain one, but still:"I'll cure it. I'll wipe that disease off the face of the planet! You'll see! I'll do it with alchemy!" Bookworm: He has quite the collection of alchemy books, as noted by Lust, but sadly lacked the talent to fully cure the fossil disease on his own. Lust ends up ripping up some of the “worthless” ones and orders him to study only a select few in order to advance his skills.

characters.name: The Gate
characters.description: The beginning and the end, the one and the all. The gateway that forms the core of the world's alchemy and the foundry of souls. It is the closest the FMA world has to a true god and a being anyone who breaks the taboo of human transmutation will have to face.Near the end of the series, it is revealed to also be a portal to a parallel world without alchemy uncannily similar to ours in real life, that uses the souls of those that die in said parallel world to fuel the alchemy of the other world. Adapted Out: Truth, the Gate's guardian in the manga, is completely absent. This somewhat serves to signify how different alchemy works in this continuity. Afterlife Antechamber: TheBlank White Voidthat the Gate resides in functions as a sort of stopover for the dead while they wait for the Gate to let them into the afterlife. As such, resurrecting a dead one is only possible while they are still in this room. Art Imitates Art: The gateway strongly resemblesThe Gates of Hellsculpture byAuguste Rodin. Blank White Void: The Gate resides in an endless empty, slightly yellow-tinted white void where those who have been put before it or the souls of the dead wait for the gate to open.

characters.name: Brothers
characters.description: Calling Parents by Their Name: Typically refers to his father as "Hohenheim," until the last chapter,when he tells Hohenheim "Shut up, you rotten father!" in response to his offering to sacrifice himself to bring Al back. Calling the Old Man Out: The first time he sees his father in the main narrative he punches the guy in the face with his metal arm. This is because he stayed away from home while Trisha wasted away and died waiting for him. Cannot Spit It Out:He'd rather recite the periodic table of elements at top speed or spitotherthings out (like his drink all over poor Black Hayate) than admit his feelings for Winry.There's his fear that Alphonse secretly blamed and hated him for the loss of his body. Ed never could bring himself to ask Al about it and it almost came back to bite him (for more on that seePoor Communication Killsunder Al's section).He also refuses to call Hohenheim his father,until the very end when Hohenheim offers to use his own body to bring Al back. He'd rather recite the periodic table of elements at top speed or spitotherthings out (like his drink all over poor Black Hayate) than admit his feelings for Winry. There's his fear that Alphonse secretly blamed and hated him for the loss of his body. Ed never could bring himself to ask Al about it and it almost came back to bite him (for more on that seePoor Communication Killsunder Al's section). Hair-Trigger Temper: You could say he has a very...shorttemper. Considering his height insecurity, he might be trying to make up for it. Handicapped Badass:Technically, but his automail usually more than compensates.At the end of the story he is still handicapped, but has both arms. Height Angst: He is so insecure about his short height that it is by far his most well-knownBerserk Button, often to the point that he'll assume any "insults" regarding it aimed in his direction are far worse than they really are.Played more subtly in a later scene between the two of them - their arguing puts them both in t

characters.name: Father
characters.description: Abusive Parents: He raises his children specifically to act as pawns in his plan and likely feels no parental attachment to them. After Greed refuses to rejoin Father's plans, he decides to melt him down to a Philosopher Stone in what looks like molten metal: possibly gold. He later resurrects Greed while purging his memories and making him kill his loved ones so Father can be his sole emotional support and focus. Although they do later come back, it shows how far Father is willing to go in order to manipulate his children. As for the rest of Homunculi, he isn't outwardly cruel but more so distant and neglectful, not caring about their inadequacies or needs. He sheds no tears when they die one by one, and before the final battle, he flees his lair while leaving Pride behind. And while Hohenheim hints he does have some care for them given that he has them call him "Father" in the first place, his selfishness outweighs any hidden feelings he has towards them. Action Dad: He's the original Homunculus, father to the seven sins, and like Hohenheim he can lay a beatdown if he feels the need to. Not that this makes him a good dad though. At all. Adaptational Sympathy:Brotherhoodplays his final fate more tragically than the Manga does. In the manga, he simply screams when the heroes watch him be absorbed by the Truth, whereas in the anime he shouts that he only wanted freedom and knowledge, followed by a reaction shot of Hohenheim looking at him in pity. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: As a sentient artificial creature that turned on humanity after being created as a mere vessel of knowledge (a computer), he technically can be considered the Alchemic equivalent. Hohenheim's master learned too late that keeping a sapient being in a jar was not a good idea. Alas, Poor Villain: InBrotherhood, and only in Hohenheim's eyes. After being absorbed by God after his defeat, Hohenheim shows pity for him as he's dying, remembering how he once used to only desire freedom from his flask. This is av
